mainTopic: Must a מצורע shave with a תער? רבי אליעזר's proof from ״ראשו״, and how the רבנן use ״ראשו״ and ״זקנו״ to override the bans on shaving
overview: The גמרא adds another proof that a מצורע must shave with a תער. If tweezers or a plane were good enough, ריש לקיש's rule would require him to use them, since that way he keeps both the עשה and the לא תעשה. Next the גמרא asks for רבי אליעזר's source and finds it in the word ״ראשו״: a נזיר מצורע shaves his head, even though a נזיר may not use a razor. The גמרא suggests the verse may only be allowing a razor, not requiring it. It then rejects that suggestion with ריש לקיש's rule, so the proof stands. Then the גמרא asks what the רבנן, who learn the razor rule from elsewhere, learn from ״ראשו״. They use it to teach that a מצורע's shaving overrides the ban on rounding the corners of the head. When the גמרא asks why ״זקנו״ is not enough, it answers that both words are needed. Without ״ראשו״ we might think shaving the whole head is not called הקפה at all. The rest of this answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Another proof that a razor is required
steps.stepSummary: If shaving with tweezers or a plane counted as the מצוה, the מצורע would never be allowed to use a תער.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: if you think that shaving with tweezers or a plane also fulfills the מצוה, then, since a razor is not written, he should not be allowed to use a razor at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second proof that a מצורע must use a תער. It is setting up an argument that it will finish with ריש לקיש's rule in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Shaving the beard with a razor is normally forbidden. If the מצורע could do his מצוה with tweezers instead, he would have no reason to break that prohibition. So the fact that the תורה lets him shave with a razor shows that a razor is the only way to do the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore; introduces an additional argument

phrases.english: And furthermore, if it should enter your mind
that when he does it with tweezers or a plane
he is performing a מצוה,
then from the fact that "razor" is not written [he should not use a razor at all],
phrases.notes: The point is that tweezers would work without breaking any prohibition, so a razor would be off limits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second proof to the earlier argument (before this section) that a מצורע must use a תער.
steps.raayaObject: That a מצורע's shaving must be done with a תער
steps.raayaSupportSource: The fact that the תורה allows the razor at all, read together with ריש לקיש's rule

steps.title: ריש לקיש's rule: keep both commands if you can
steps.stepSummary: When an עשה clashes with a לא תעשה, you should keep both if possible. Only if that is impossible does the עשה push aside the לא תעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As ריש לקיש said: Wherever you find a positive command and a prohibition that clash, if you can fulfill both, that is best. If not, the positive command comes and overrides the prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes ריש לקיש's general rule, which completes the proof from step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עשה only pushes aside a לא תעשה when there is no way to keep both. Applied here: if tweezers worked, the מצורע could keep both commands, so using a razor would not be allowed. Since the תורה does allow a razor, tweezers must not count.

keyTerms.meaning: A positive command (something you must do)
A prohibition (something you must not do)
The positive command comes and overrides

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is used all over the תלמוד. An עשה pushes aside a לא תעשה only as a last resort.

phrases.english: in accordance with Reish Lakish, who said:
Any place where you find
a positive command and a prohibition [clashing],

phrases.aramaic: אִם אַתָּה יָכוֹל לְקַיֵּים אֶת שְׁנֵיהֶם —
phrases.english: if you are able to fulfill both of them,
that is best; and if not,

phrases.aramaic: יָבֹא עֲשֵׂה וְיִדְחֶה אֶת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה.
phrases.english: let the positive command come and override the prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁאַתָּה מוֹצֵא עֲשֵׂה וְלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the general rule that makes the step 1 proof work.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Keep both the עשה and the לא תעשה when possible; the עשה overrides only when you cannot keep both.

steps.title: Where does רבי אליעזר learn the razor rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what source רבי אליעזר uses to show that a מצורע shaves with a razor.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר, what is his reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רבי אליעזר and asks for his source. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר also holds that a מצורע uses a תער. The גמרא wants to know which verse he learns it from.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer, what is his reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the earlier proofs to רבי אליעזר's own source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The verse from which רבי אליעזר learns that a מצורע must use a תער

steps.title: He learns it from the word "his head"
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the word ״ראשו״ makes a נזיר who is a מצורע shave his head, even though a נזיר is normally forbidden to use a razor.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from "his head." As a ברייתא teaches: Why does the verse say "his head"? Since it says about a נזיר, "A razor shall not pass over his head," you might think a נזיר who is a מצורע is also forbidden. So the verse says "his head" to teach that he does shave it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: רבי אליעזר learns it from the word ״ראשו״, as explained in a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר is only forbidden to shave with a razor. If a מצורע could use tweezers, the נזיר מצורע would simply use tweezers and never need permission. So the verse permitting a נזיר מצורע to shave his head shows that a מצורע must use a razor.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the verse need to say this?
A נזיר who is also a מצורע

phrases.english: He learns it from "his head."
As it is taught: "His head" — why does the verse say it?
Because it is said regarding a nazir:
"A razor shall not pass over his head,"
one might think a nazir who is a metzora is also so [forbidden to shave],
therefore the verse says: "his head."

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From ״ראשו״: a נזיר מצורע must shave his head, which only makes sense if the shaving must be done with a תער.

steps.title: Maybe tweezers also count
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the proof: perhaps removing the hair with tweezers or a plane also fulfills the מצורע's מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do you know this? Perhaps even if he removed the hair with tweezers or a plane, he still performs the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from ״ראשו״. It suggests that other tools might also work for a מצורע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof from step 4 only works if the verse requires a razor. The גמרא points out that this was never shown. Tweezers might be fine too.

phrases.english: From where [do you know this]? Perhaps really
even if he removed it with tweezers or a plane,
he is performing a מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion drawn from the ברייתא in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from ״ראשו״ that a razor is required
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The verse may only permit the razor rather than require it.

steps.title: Then why mention the razor at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא anticipates an objection: if tweezers work, why would the verse need to deal with a razor?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: Then why do I need the teaching about a razor?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible objection to its own pushback. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר is only forbidden to shave with a תער. If tweezers were fine, a verse permitting the נזיר מצורע to shave seems pointless, because he could just use tweezers.

phrases.english: And if you will say: Why do I need [the teaching about] a razor?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises an objection to the pushback of step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion in step 5 that tweezers suffice
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If tweezers suffice, the verse permitting a נזיר מצורע to shave would seem unnecessary.

steps.title: The verse only allows a razor, it does not require one
steps.stepSummary: The verse is needed to teach that a נזיר מצורע is not liable if he shaves with a razor. You might have thought he is liable, just like any נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches that even a razor is allowed. You might have thought: since a נזיר is liable when he shaves with a razor, a נזיר מצורע should be liable too. So the verse teaches that he is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection. The verse is needed to permit a razor, not to require one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the verse, we would have said the נזיר מצורע is liable for using a razor, like any נזיר. The verse removes that liability. If that were right, the verse would have a purpose even if tweezers also worked, so it would not prove that a razor is required. The next step rejects this.
steps.whatToRemember: At this stage, ״ראשו״ seems to teach only that a razor is allowed for a נזיר מצורע, not that it is required. The next step rejects this answer and restores the proof for רבי אליעזר.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse "allowed to use a razor" with "required to use a razor." The whole rejection depends on that difference.

phrases.english: To say that even with a razor [it is allowed].
It would have entered your mind to say,
since regarding a nazir,
when he does it with a razor he is liable,
regarding a metzora too he should be liable,
phrases.notes: He means a נזיר who is also a מצורע and shaves for his purification.

phrases.english: so it teaches us that he is not!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 6, which keeps the rejection of step 5 standing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the verse a different purpose (permission rather than requirement)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A נזיר מצורע who shaves with a razor would be liable like any נזיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse teaches that he is not liable, so a razor is permitted, but it is not shown to be required.

steps.title: If tweezers counted, a razor would be forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that tweezers fulfill the מצוה. If they did, then by ריש לקיש's rule the נזיר מצורע could never use a razor. So the verse must be teaching that a razor is required.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think that using tweezers or a plane counts as the מצוה, then since the verse did not write 'razor,' he would not be allowed to use one, following ריש לקיש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the answer from step 7 and brings back the original proof for רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש teaches that if you can keep both a מצוה and a לאו, you may not break the לאו. If tweezers worked, the נזיר could shave with tweezers and never break his ban on a razor, so the תורה would never let him use a razor. The verse ״ראשו״ does allow the razor, so it must be that only a razor fulfills the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: A plane, a carpenter's smoothing tool

steps.whyThisMatters: This step firmly sets up רבי אליעזר's view that a מצורע must shave with a razor.

phrases.english: If it should enter your mind
that when he does it with tweezers or a plane
he is doing the מצוה
then since the verse did not write 'razor'
[he could not use one], like ריש לקיש.
phrases.notes: ריש לקיש's rule: if you can keep both the מצוה and the prohibition, you have to.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 7 and restores the proof from step 4
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that tweezers or a plane fulfill the מצוה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: If tweezers worked, ריש לקיש's rule would forbid a razor, and then the verse would have no reason to permit one

steps.title: What do the רבנן learn from ״ראשו״?
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן learn the razor rule from a different source, so the גמרא asks what they learn from the word ״ראשו״.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן: what do they learn from this word 'his head'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the רבנן, who learn the razor rule from a different verse than רבי אליעזר, and asks what the word ״ראשו״ teaches according to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר used ״ראשו״ to prove that a razor is required. The רבנן reach the same rule from a different source, so they do not need ״ראשו״ for it. The גמרא asks what job the word does in their view.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, who argue with רבי אליעזר
They expound, meaning they learn a lesson from a word

phrases.english: And the Rabbis,
this word 'his head',
what do they learn from it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי אליעזר's reading of the word to the רבנן's reading
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson the רבנן learn from ״ראשו״

steps.title: 'His head' overrides the ban on rounding
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן use ״ראשו״ to teach that a מצורע's shaving overrides the לאו of הקפת הראש, rounding the corners of the head.
steps.simpleTranslation: They need it to override the prohibition of rounding. As a ברייתא teaches: 'Do not round the corners of your head.' You might think a מצורע is included too, so the verse says 'his head.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that for the רבנן, ״ראשו״ teaches that a מצורע may shave his whole head, even the corners that are normally forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every man is forbidden to shave off the corners of his head. A מצורע has to shave all his hair, which includes those corners. The word ״ראשו״ tells us that his מצוה pushes aside that לאו.

keyTerms.meaning: The prohibition of rounding off the corners of the head
The corners of your head, meaning the sideburn area

phrases.english: They need it
to push aside the prohibition of rounding.
As it was taught:
'You shall not round the corners of your head.'
One might think that a מצורע is the same,
so the verse says: 'his head.'

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For the רבנן, ״ראשו״ teaches that a מצורע's shaving overrides the לאו of הקפה

steps.title: Why not learn it from 'his beard'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this: the word ״זקנו״ already teaches that a מצורע's shaving overrides a ban on shaving, so why is ״ראשו״ needed?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need it to write 'his head'? Learn it from 'his beard.' As a ברייתא teaches: Why does the verse say 'his beard'? Because it says 'they shall not shave the corners of their beard,' you might think a מצורע is the same, so the verse says 'his beard.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא argues that ״ראשו״ is extra, since ״זקנו״ already shows that a מצורע's shaving overrides a לאו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא already learns from ״זקנו״ that the מצורע's shaving overrides the ban on shaving the beard. If his מצוה overrides one ban, it should override the ban on rounding the head too. So it looks like ״ראשו״ teaches nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him derive it instead from...

phrases.english: Why do I need it to write 'his head'?
Let him derive it from 'his beard'!
As it was taught:
'His beard': why does the verse say it?
Because it says
'And the corners of their beard they shall not shave,'
one might think that a מצורע is the same,
so the verse says: 'his beard.'

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמָה לִי לְמִכְתַּב ״רֹאשׁוֹ״? וְתִיפּוֹק לֵיהּ מִ״זְּקָנוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the derivation of step 10 as unnecessary
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of ״ראשו״ to override the לאו of הקפה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ״זקנו״ already shows that a מצורע's shaving overrides a לאו, so ״ראשו״ seems extra

steps.title: Why write both words?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sharpens the question: why does the Torah need to write both ״ראשו״ and ״זקנו״?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need it to write 'his head,' and why do I need it to write 'his beard'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא restates the challenge in a sharper form and sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both words teach the same idea, that a מצורע's shaving overrides a לאו. So one of them seems to be extra. The גמרא now asks why each one is needed.

phrases.english: Why do I need it to write 'his head'
and why do I need it to write 'his beard'?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמָה לִי לְמִכְתַּב ״רֹאשׁוֹ״ וּלְמָה לִי לְמִכְתַּב ״זְקָנוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the challenge of step 11 into a question about why both verses are written
steps.kashyaTarget: Having two verses, ״ראשו״ and ״זקנו״, that seem to teach the same thing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One verse should be enough to teach that a מצורע's shaving overrides a לאו

steps.title: Both words are needed
steps.stepSummary: Both words are needed. From ״זקנו״ alone we might think that shaving the whole head is not called הקפה at all, so ״ראשו״ teaches that it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are both needed. If the Torah had written only 'his beard' and not 'his head,' I would have said that rounding the entire head is not called rounding. That is why the Torah wrote 'his head.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with צריכי and explains here why ״ראשו״ is needed even though ״זקנו״ is written. The other half of the צריכותא continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without ״ראשו״, we might think that shaving the entire head is not the forbidden kind of הקפה, since the לאו is about the corners. If so, the מצורע would not be breaking any ban, and ״זקנו״ would tell us nothing about the head. ״ראשו״ teaches that shaving the whole head really is הקפה, and that the מצוה overrides it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
I would have thought (a mistaken first idea)
Rounding, that is shaving, the entire head

steps.confusionAlert: ״ראשו״ does not teach that shaving the whole head is allowed for everyone. It teaches the opposite: shaving the whole head is real הקפה, and only the מצורע's מצוה overrides it.

phrases.english: They are both needed.
For if the Merciful One had written 'his beard'
and had not written 'his head',
I would have said:
rounding the entire head
is not called rounding.
That is why the Merciful One wrote 'his head'.

steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each verse is needed for its own lesson
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From ״זקנו״ alone, one would think that shaving the entire head is not considered הקפה at all
steps.terutzMaskana: ״ראשו״ teaches that shaving the whole head is real הקפה, and that the מצורע's מצוה overrides it
